LogBook: Brainstorming problem statement for SAT project. Identified the 'Panic Gap' issue in school workshops and established project constraints.
Finalizing the requirements and considerations. Decided on a dual-microcontroller architecture (Pi + Arduino) to hit the complexity constraint.
Researching existing solutions like wall kits, vending spirals, and smart pill dispensers to inform my design.
Literature review on UART serial communication and Rack & Pinion kinematics for linear dispensing.
Brainstorming and writing up alternative design options (Option 2: Voice Carousel & Option 3: RFID Solenoid).
Fleshing out the preferred option (AI Rack & Pinion) and comparing all 3 options in a selection matrix.
Starting Fusion 360 CAD for the 3D printed smart cartridge. Set up user parameters for width, height, and tolerances.
Finished CAD modeling of the rack, pinion, pusher sled, and the exterior 6mm plywood chassis with the 45-degree ramp.
Designing the electronic control system and deciding on exact components (Raspberry Pi 4, Arduino Uno, FS90R Servos).
Creating the IPO Block Diagram, pseudocode flowchart, and completing the Risk Assessment for tools and equipment.
Finalizing materials list, costing spreadsheet ($322.25 total), and developing the estimated vs actual Gantt chart timeline.
Final review of the SAT Part A Folio. Updated the executive summary, evaluated factors, and created the visual evidence checklist.
Term 2 starts. Began setting up the Raspberry Pi 4. Installed Raspberry Pi OS (Linux).
Encountered major issues connecting the Raspberry Pi to the school's Wi-Fi network due to restrictive enterprise firewall (802.1x EAP).
Still troubleshooting Pi network issues. Attempted MAC address spoofing and installing custom CA certificates for the school network.
Finally resolved Pi network issue by bridging the connection through my laptop's mobile hotspot for initial package downloads.
Began Python development on the Pi. Installed required libraries (pyserial, requests) for the Gemini API and Arduino communication.
Began electronics setup. Soldered header pins to the Arduino Uno and wired the FS90R servo and limit switch to a breadboard.
Wrote initial C++ test script for the Arduino. Successfully spun the servo and stopped it using the limit switch interrupt.
Successfully established UART serial communication between the Pi and Arduino. Sent a string from Python and read it in C++.
Drafting the Gemini API prompt. Testing how to force the AI to return a strict '010' binary format instead of conversational text.
Connected the USB microphone to the Pi. Testing audio capture and saving to .wav files using Python.
Integrating the audio capture with the Gemini API script. Successfully sent a recorded voice file to the API and received a response.
Combined the AI Python script with the Serial output script. The Pi now listens, processes via AI, and commands the Arduino automatically.
Software foundation complete. Shifting to hardware. Sent initial CAD files to the Prusa 3D printers for the first PoC cartridge and sled.
Removed 3D prints from the bed. Conducted a physical tolerance test with a real bandage packet. Found the sled was too tight.
Term 2 ends. Documenting the networking errors and the sled tightness issues into the official Project Fix Log.
Term 3 starts. Adjusted Fusion 360 parameters for the sled width. Discovered the gear rack wasn't long enough to push the bandage fully out.
Extended the gear rack length in CAD to 110mm. Designed a custom involute pinion gear specifically matched to the FS90R servo spline.
Printed the new elongated rack and custom pinion gear. Assembled the physical mechanism. Slides smoother, but teeth are skipping.
Debugging gear alignment. The custom pinion gear is slightly too small, causing it to slip on the rack under load.
Currently adjusting the module (mod) spacing of the involute gear in Fusion 360 to ensure tighter meshing with the rack before next test.
Used a custom Python script (generate.py) via Fusion 360 API to parametrically extend the linear rack from 95mm to 120mm (26 teeth).
Printed the elongated rack and new 12-tooth pinion. Tolerance is perfect (1.5mm). Rack now achieves 118.5mm of linear stroke.
Latency issues detected with Python on Pi 4 during 16kHz audio downmixing. Decided to upgrade hardware to Raspberry Pi 5 (8GB) for multi-core headroom.
Scrapped Python architecture. Rewrote main logic in Rust (2024 Edition). Achieved sub-microsecond JSON deserialization and eliminated garbage collection spikes.
Updated Arduino C++ firmware. Added 'servo.detach()' after the push/retract cycle to completely eliminate idle micro-jitter and coil heating.
Fabricated 5V 3A power distribution rail with 1000uF decoupling capacitors. Wore safety glasses and used fume extractor to comply with OH&S.
Consolidated from 3 to 2 cartridges (Bandages & Alcohol). De-scoped plywood chassis for an Open-Frame Benchtop Test-Rig to allow easy diagnostic probing.
Completed physical assembly of the open-frame rig. Mounted the Pi 5, Arduino Uno, and both PLA cartridges. Wired up the star-ground configuration.
Diagnostic Test 2: Ran automated Python protocol suite (48/48 passed). Tested Gemini Vision logic with 10 images (100% on clear, 0% on blur).
Diagnostic Test 3: Mechanical ejection. 80% success rate (2 jams). Identified friction issue at the 2.5mm slit. Planned to widen slit and sand baseplate.
Diagnostic Test 1: End-to-end latency testing. Mean response 15.1s. Transitioned Pi 5 to a dedicated 5GHz mobile hotspot to bypass school Wi-Fi firewall latency.
Compiled test data, populated Criteria Evaluation matrices, and finalized the Plan vs Reality comparison for the Part B folio.
Filmed final full-loop operational trial video. Formatted references and Generative AI prompts into Appendix A. Final PDF export for submission.
